_note: effective_vuln = vuln × (1 − diff).  ALE = LEF × loss_magnitude.  control_benefit is computed server-side from proposed_control.

scenarios.name: Ransomware — Core Banking Infrastructure
scenarios.description: Threat actor deploys ransomware targeting core banking and payment processing systems, causing multi-day operational outage, recovery costs, and potential regulatory fines.

proposed_control.name: Enhanced EDR + 24/7 MDR Retainer
proposed_control.description: Deploy next-gen endpoint detection & response across all servers and workstations with a 24/7 managed detection and response retainer and pre-negotiated IR playbook.

scenarios.name: Data Breach — Customer PII & Financial Records
scenarios.description: Unauthorized exfiltration of customer personally identifiable information and financial records via compromised credentials or SQL injection, triggering regulatory penalties and litigation.

proposed_control.name: CASB + DLP + Privileged Access Management
proposed_control.description: Implement Cloud Access Security Broker, enterprise Data Loss Prevention, and Privileged Access Management to reduce data exfiltration risk and limit blast radius of credential compromise.

scenarios.name: Business Email Compromise — Wire Fraud
scenarios.description: Social engineering attack targeting treasury and finance staff to authorise fraudulent wire transfers to attacker-controlled accounts. High frequency, low per-event success rate.

proposed_control.name: Email Security Gateway + Security Awareness Training
proposed_control.description: Deploy advanced email security with impersonation detection, DMARC/DKIM enforcement, and a quarterly security awareness training program with BEC-specific simulations.

scenarios.name: Insider Threat — Data Exfiltration by Privileged User
scenarios.description: Malicious employee or contractor with privileged database or system access exfiltrates sensitive financial records, customer PII, or trading data for personal gain or competitive espionage.
scenarios.asset: Financial Records, Customer Data, Trading Systems

proposed_control.name: UEBA + Zero-Trust Privileged Access
proposed_control.description: Deploy User & Entity Behaviour Analytics with anomaly alerts on sensitive data access patterns, combined with just-in-time privileged access controls and session recording.

scenarios.name: Third-Party / Supply Chain Attack — Fintech Vendor
scenarios.description: Compromise through a trusted fintech partner, core banking software provider, or managed IT/security vendor gives the attacker persistent access to internal systems with minimal detection.

proposed_control.name: Vendor Risk Management Platform + Contractual Controls
proposed_control.description: Implement continuous vendor security assessment platform with mandatory SOC 2 Type II attestation, network segmentation for third-party integrations, and real-time vendor threat intelligence feeds.

scenarios.name: Ransomware — Electronic Health Record Systems
scenarios.description: Ransomware encrypts EHR, clinical imaging, and connected medical device systems, forcing diversion of emergency patients, manual processes, and triggering HIPAA breach notification obligations.
scenarios.asset: EHR, Clinical Imaging & Medical Device Networks

proposed_control.name: Healthcare EDR + Segmented Backup + IR Retainer
proposed_control.description: Deploy healthcare-specific endpoint protection across clinical and administrative devices, implement immutable offline backups for EHR data, and retain a healthcare-specialized incident response firm.

scenarios.name: Data Breach — Protected Health Information (PHI)
scenarios.description: Unauthorized access to or exfiltration of Protected Health Information triggering HIPAA breach notification, OCR investigation, class-action litigation, and severe reputational damage.

proposed_control.name: PHI Data Governance + HIPAA Compliance Suite
proposed_control.description: Implement a PHI data classification and governance platform with automated de-identification controls, multi-factor authentication on all EHR access, and continuous HIPAA compliance monitoring.

scenarios.name: Business Email Compromise — Billing & Vendor Payments
scenarios.description: Spear-phishing targeting billing coordinators or C-suite executives to redirect vendor payments, insurance reimbursements, or grant funding to attacker-controlled accounts.

proposed_control.name: DMARC Enforcement + Clinical Staff Phishing Training
proposed_control.description: Enforce DMARC/DKIM/SPF on all email domains, deploy advanced anti-phishing gateway, and deliver quarterly phishing simulation campaigns with clinical and administrative staff-specific content.

scenarios.name: Insider Threat — Patient Data Theft
scenarios.description: Clinician, administrator, or contractor accesses patient records without authorisation — for identity theft, insurance fraud, or sale on dark-web marketplaces — triggering HIPAA enforcement and litigation.

proposed_control.name: PHI Access Controls + PAM + User Behaviour Analytics
proposed_control.description: Implement role-based PHI access with need-to-know enforcement, privileged access management for admin accounts, and user behaviour analytics to detect anomalous patient record access patterns.

scenarios.name: Third-Party / Supply Chain — Medical Device & SaaS Vendor
scenarios.description: Compromise through a connected medical device manufacturer, healthcare SaaS platform, or managed service provider used across clinical and administrative operations.

proposed_control.name: Healthcare Vendor Security Assessment Program
proposed_control.description: Mandate HITRUST or SOC 2 Type II for all clinical SaaS vendors, deploy medical device network isolation, and establish a continuous vendor threat intelligence and monitoring capability.

scenarios.name: Ransomware — Development & Cloud Operations
scenarios.description: Ransomware deployment across CI/CD pipelines, developer workstations, and cloud operations infrastructure, causing build system outages, potential source code encryption, and customer SLA breaches.

proposed_control.name: Immutable Backups + Zero-Trust Network Segmentation
proposed_control.description: Deploy immutable build artifact and source code backups, implement zero-trust micro-segmentation to isolate development from production environments, and extend EDR to all developer endpoints.

scenarios.name: Data Breach — Customer Platform & Cloud Data
scenarios.description: Exposed cloud storage, misconfigured IAM, or API vulnerability leads to unauthorized access to customer data stored in the SaaS platform, triggering regulatory and contractual obligations.

proposed_control.name: Cloud Security Posture Mgmt + Data Security Posture Mgmt
proposed_control.description: Deploy CSPM to eliminate cloud misconfigurations, implement DSPM to discover and classify sensitive customer data, and enforce least-privilege IAM with automated policy drift detection.

scenarios.name: Business Email Compromise — Finance & Procurement
scenarios.description: Spear-phishing targeting finance or procurement staff to redirect vendor invoices or intercept software licensing payments. Often exploits remote-work email culture.

proposed_control.name: Advanced Email Gateway + Executive Impersonation Detection
proposed_control.description: Deploy AI-powered email security with executive impersonation detection, enforce DMARC on all company domains, and implement a two-person approval rule for wire transfers over $25K.

scenarios.name: Insider Threat — IP Theft by Departing Engineer
scenarios.description: Departing software engineer or researcher exfiltrates proprietary source code, ML models, or product roadmaps before resignation, enabling competitive harm or direct sale.
scenarios.asset: Source Code, ML Models & R&D Intellectual Property

proposed_control.name: Source Code DLP + Git Access Reviews + UEBA
proposed_control.description: Deploy code repository DLP to detect mass downloads and unusual commit patterns, enforce quarterly access reviews on all source repositories, and monitor developer behaviour with UEBA for early-warning signals.

scenarios.name: Third-Party / Supply Chain — Software Dependency Compromise
scenarios.description: Malicious code injected into an open-source library, CI/CD plugin, or infrastructure-as-code module used in the build pipeline, allowing attackers to reach production customer environments.

proposed_control.name: SBOM + Software Supply Chain Security Platform
proposed_control.description: Generate and continuously monitor Software Bills of Materials for all dependencies, enforce package signing and provenance verification in CI/CD, and deploy a dedicated supply chain security scanning platform.
